title: Unique Paths
description: A robot starts at the top-left of an `m` by `n` grid and may move only right or down. Return the number of distinct paths to the bottom-right cell.
hints: Define the state as the best answer for a prefix or cell.
Update from the previous row or previous prefix while preserving the recurrence.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public int uniquePaths(int m,int n) { int[] d=new int[n]; java.util.Arrays.fill(d,1); for(int i=1;i<m;i++)for(int j=1;j<n;j++)d[j]+=d[j-1]; return d[n-1]; } }

title: Unique Paths II
description: A robot starts at the top-left of a grid and may move only right or down. A cell containing 1 is blocked; 0 is open. Return the number of paths to the bottom-right cell. If the start or finish is blocked, return 0.
constraints: The number of valid paths fits in a signed 32-bit integer.
hints: Define a dynamic-programming state for each prefix of the inputs.
Update each state using only valid preceding states and the allowed transitions.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public int uniquePathsWithObstacles(int[][] g) { int[] d=new int[g[0].length];d[0]=1;for(int[] row:g)for(int j=0;j<row.length;j++){if(row[j]==1)d[j]=0;else if(j>0)d[j]+=d[j-1];}return d[d.length-1];} }

title: Minimum Path Sum
description: Given a grid of non-negative costs, start at the top-left and reach the bottom-right by moving only right or down. Return the minimum possible sum of the visited cells, including both endpoints.
hints: Define the state as the best answer for a prefix or cell.
Update from the previous row or previous prefix while preserving the recurrence.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public int minPathSum(int[][] g) { int m=g.length,n=g[0].length; int[] d=g[0].clone(); for(int i=1;i<m;i++){d[0]+=g[i][0];for(int j=1;j<n;j++)d[j]=Math.min(d[j],d[j-1])+g[i][j];}return d[n-1]; } }

title: Edit Distance
description: Return the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions, or substitutions needed to transform `word1` into `word2`.
hints: Define the state as the best answer for a prefix or cell.
Update from the previous row or previous prefix while preserving the recurrence.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public int minDistance(String a,String b) { int[] d=new int[b.length()+1];for(int j=0;j<=b.length();j++)d[j]=j;for(int i=1;i<=a.length();i++){int prev=d[0];d[0]=i;for(int j=1;j<=b.length();j++){int old=d[j];d[j]=a.charAt(i-1)==b.charAt(j-1)?prev:1+Math.min(prev,Math.min(d[j],d[j-1]));prev=old;}}return d[b.length()]; } }

title: Longest Common Subsequence
description: Return the length of the longest sequence of characters that appears in both strings in the same relative order. The characters in a subsequence need not be contiguous.
hints: Define the state as the best answer for a prefix or cell.
Update from the previous row or previous prefix while preserving the recurrence.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public int longestCommonSubsequence(String a,String b) { int[] d=new int[b.length()+1]; for(int i=0;i<a.length();i++){int prev=0;for(int j=1;j<=b.length();j++){int old=d[j];d[j]=a.charAt(i)==b.charAt(j-1)?prev+1:Math.max(d[j],d[j-1]);prev=old;}}return d[b.length()]; } }

title: Interleaving String
description: Return true if `s3` can be formed by interleaving `s1` and `s2` while preserving the order of characters from each source string. Every character in each source must be used exactly once.
hints: Define a dynamic-programming state for each prefix of the inputs.
Update each state using only valid preceding states and the allowed transitions.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public boolean isInterleave(String a,String b,String c) { if(a.length()+b.length()!=c.length())return false;boolean[] d=new boolean[b.length()+1];d[0]=true;for(int j=1;j<=b.length();j++)d[j]=d[j-1]&&b.charAt(j-1)==c.charAt(j-1);for(int i=1;i<=a.length();i++){d[0]=d[0]&&a.charAt(i-1)==c.charAt(i-1);for(int j=1;j<=b.length();j++)d[j]=(d[j]&&a.charAt(i-1)==c.charAt(i+j-1))||(d[j-1]&&b.charAt(j-1)==c.charAt(i+j-1));}return d[b.length()];} }

title: Distinct Subsequences
description: Return the number of distinct subsequences of `s` that equal `t`. A subsequence is formed by deleting zero or more characters without changing the order of the remaining characters.
constraints: s and t contain lowercase English letters
The answer fits in a signed 64-bit integer
hints: Define a dynamic-programming state for each prefix of the inputs.
Update each state using only valid preceding states and the allowed transitions.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public long numDistinct(String s,String t) { long[] d=new long[t.length()+1];d[0]=1;for(int i=0;i<s.length();i++)for(int j=t.length()-1;j>=0;j--)if(s.charAt(i)==t.charAt(j))d[j+1]+=d[j];return d[t.length()];} }

title: Maximal Square
description: Given a binary matrix, return the area of the largest square containing only 1s. Return 0 if the matrix contains no 1s.
hints: Define the state as the best answer for a prefix or cell.
Update from the previous row or previous prefix while preserving the recurrence.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public int maximalSquare(int[][] a) { int n=a[0].length,best=0;int[] d=new int[n+1];for(int[] row:a){int prev=0;for(int j=1;j<=n;j++){int old=d[j];d[j]=row[j-1]==1?1+Math.min(d[j],Math.min(d[j-1],prev)):0;best=Math.max(best,d[j]);prev=old;}}return best*best;} }

title: Dungeon Game
description: A knight starts at the top-left of a dungeon and must reach the bottom-right, moving only right or down. Each cell adds or removes health. Find the minimum starting health that guarantees the knight’s health stays at least 1 at every step.
hints: Define a dynamic-programming state for each prefix of the inputs.
Update each state using only valid preceding states and the allowed transitions.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public int calculateMinimumHP(int[][] a) { int m=a.length,n=a[0].length;long[] d=new long[n+1];Arrays.fill(d,Long.MAX_VALUE/4);d[n-1]=1;for(int i=m-1;i>=0;i--)for(int j=n-1;j>=0;j--)d[j]=Math.max(1,Math.min(d[j],d[j+1])-a[i][j]);return (int)d[0];} }

title: Wildcard Matching
description: Return true if pattern `p` matches all of string `s`. `?` matches exactly one character, and `*` matches any sequence of characters, including an empty sequence. All other pattern characters match themselves.
constraints: s and p contain lowercase letters, ? or *
hints: Define a dynamic-programming state for each prefix of the inputs.
Update each state using only valid preceding states and the allowed transitions.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public boolean isMatch(String s,String p) { boolean[] d=new boolean[p.length()+1];d[0]=true;for(int j=1;j<=p.length();j++)d[j]=d[j-1]&&p.charAt(j-1)=='*';for(int i=0;i<s.length();i++){boolean[] n=new boolean[p.length()+1];for(int j=1;j<=p.length();j++){char c=p.charAt(j-1);if(c=='*')n[j]=n[j-1]||d[j];else n[j]=d[j-1]&&(c=='?'||c==s.charAt(i));}d=n;}return d[p.length()];} }
